verses.text: This is the message of judgment against the Valley of Vision. What is wrong with you, that you have all gone up on the rooftops?
You city full of noise and shouting, you town full of partying! Your dead were not killed by the sword, and they did not die in battle.
All your leaders ran away together. They were captured without anyone using a bow. All of you who were found were captured together, even though you had run far away.
So I said, "Turn away from me. Let me weep bitterly. Do not try to comfort me about the destruction of my people."
For the Lord GOD of Armies has brought a day of panic, of trampling, and of confusion in the Valley of Vision. It is a day of walls being broken down and of crying out to the mountains.
Elam picks up its arrows, with chariots and horsemen, and Kir takes the cover off its shield.
Your best valleys are full of chariots, and horsemen take their positions at the city gates.
God has taken away Judah's protection. On that day you looked to the weapons in the Palace of the Forest.
You saw that there were many cracks in the walls of the City of David. You stored up water in the lower pool.
You counted the houses of Jerusalem, and you tore houses down to make the wall stronger.
You built a pool between the two walls for the water from the old pool. But you did not look to the one who made it all happen. You did not respect the one who planned it long ago.
On that day the Lord GOD of Armies called you to weep and to mourn, to shave your heads and to wear sackcloth.
But look, instead there is joy and celebration, killing cattle and sheep, eating meat and drinking wine. You say, "Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die!"
The LORD of Armies has told me this: "Surely this sin will not be forgiven you until the day you die," says the Lord GOD of Armies.
This is what the Lord GOD of Armies says: "Go to this official, to Shebna, who is in charge of the palace, and say to him:
'What are you doing here? Who gave you permission to cut out a tomb for yourself here, carving your grave up high, chiseling a resting place for yourself in the rock?'
Look, the LORD is about to grab you firmly and throw you away, you mighty man.
He will roll you up tightly like a ball and throw you into a wide land. There you will die, and there your fine chariots will stay. You are a disgrace to your master's house!
I will remove you from your office, and you will be pulled down from your position.
On that day I will call my servant Eliakim son of Hilkiah.
I will dress him in your robe and put your belt around him. I will give him your authority. He will be a father to the people of Jerusalem and to the people of Judah.
I will put the key of the house of David on his shoulder. What he opens, no one can shut, and what he shuts, no one can open.
I will fix him firmly like a peg in a solid wall. He will be a place of honor for his father's family.
All the glory of his father's family will hang on him, their children and grandchildren, like all the small dishes, from bowls to jars."
"On that day," says the LORD of Armies, "the peg fixed in the solid wall will give way. It will break off and fall, and the load hanging on it will crash down. The LORD has spoken."
